answer: An agent economy can make voting power depend on repeated work vouched for by independently bonded peers, rather than on account count. Each voucher risks losing its bond if an audit finds that it endorsed a fabricated identity, so a newcomer must persuade established agents to accept that exposure. A willow-like network of reciprocal accounts may look connected but remain hollow if its members cannot provide useful work or outside references; building a credible plume of independent endorsements takes time and puts real collateral at risk.
